calls.reason: DigitalToday supports the 89% figure only for a restricted startup sample using annualised revenue. It does not establish the $20 billion ceiling for the rest of the industry.

TrendForce supports AI-driven memory price pressure, and The Buildout reports a $100 billion estimate. Neither establishes comparable costs doubling within ten months or attributes that doubling to memory and storage.

OpenAI's financing announcement and PYMNTS's cash-burn report show reliance on outside capital, but do not establish the estimated 70% share. Epoch measures compute capacity, not revenue or funding flows.

Microsoft reports 26% RPO growth excluding OpenAI, weakening the surrounding argument. But the hyperscaler disclosures do not establish the two labs' combined share or isolate the scale of other AI compute demand.

NVIDIA's August disclosure reports growing data-center revenue and a supply-constrained outlook. The packet does not establish the forecast's capex-and-demand trigger or the subsequent semiconductor downturn.
The hedged 2026 forecast still has time remaining. Anthropic's filing shows $16.3 billion in first-half revenue, but supplies neither combined full-year revenue nor combined compute spending.
